ip_top_stories.title: Authors Sue Meta's AI Scientists Directly in Llama Copyright Case
ip_top_stories.summary: Authors have escalated their copyright litigation by suing Meta's AI scientists personally in the ongoing Llama copyright case. The move marks a significant legal development, targeting individuals rather than just the corporation over alleged use of copyrighted works in AI training.

ip_top_stories.title: UMG and Sony seek to add over 61k recordings to Suno lawsuit after discovery reveals AI trained on 'millions' of their copyrighted tracks
ip_top_stories.summary: Universal Music Group and Sony Music are seeking to dramatically expand their lawsuit against AI music generator Suno, adding over 61,000 recordings after discovery proceedings allegedly revealed the AI was trained on millions of their copyrighted tracks. The development signals a significant escalation in the music industry's legal campaign against generative AI platforms.

ip_top_stories.title: Sony Music Files to Expand Udio Suit, Alleges 30K Infringed Works
ip_top_stories.summary: Sony Music is filing to expand its copyright lawsuit against AI music generator Udio, alleging infringement of approximately 30,000 works. The move parallels Sony and UMG's expansion of the Suno case and reflects a broad industry push to hold AI music platforms accountable for large-scale copyright infringement.

ip_top_stories.title: AI Firms Can't Shake Disney, WB's Copyright Suit
ip_top_stories.summary: A US court has denied MiniMax's bid to dismiss copyright infringement claims brought by Disney and Warner Bros. over its AI system, allowing the case to proceed. The ruling is a setback for AI companies seeking early dismissal of major studio copyright claims.

ip_top_stories.title: Eisner Awards to Implement AI Policy Following Controversy [Metered]
ip_top_stories.summary: The Eisner Awards will implement a new AI policy after a nominated anthology was withdrawn amid controversy over AI-generated content. The episode highlights growing pressure on literary and arts awards to address AI disclosure and eligibility standards.

ip_further_links.title: Europe's Copyright Trap Stalls AI Ambitions - Center for European Policy Analysis (CEPA)
ip_further_links.summary: CEPA argues that Europe's existing copyright framework is creating friction for AI development, potentially hampering the region's competitiveness in the global AI race.

ip_further_links.title: Australian creatives urge the government to 'hold the line' on AI and copyright law
ip_further_links.summary: Australian creative industry groups are calling on the government to resist pressure to relax copyright protections in the context of AI training and use.

ip_further_links.title: Artist Sues Copyright Office Over its Refusal to Register His AI-Enhanced Photo
ip_further_links.summary: An artist has filed suit against the US Copyright Office after it declined to register a photograph he enhanced using AI, raising questions about the boundaries of human authorship and AI-assisted works.

ip_further_links.title: Can you own a voice? Taylor Swift's latest legal move raises big questions for AI and copyright
ip_further_links.summary: Taylor Swift's legal action over her vocal likeness is prompting broader debate about whether AI-generated voice clones can be protected or restricted under existing copyright and trademark law.

ip_further_links.title: Japan eyes rules to regulate AI summaries' 'free riding' on news
ip_further_links.summary: Japan is considering new regulations to address AI systems that summarise news content without compensation, as publishers push back against what they describe as free riding on their journalism.

ip_further_links.title: Media orgs push back against the relaxation of federal government's stance on AI, copyright
ip_further_links.summary: Media organisations are opposing moves by the US federal government to soften copyright protections in relation to AI training, arguing it would harm creators and publishers.

ip_further_links.title: Legal Risk Could Deflate the GenAI Bubble
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis argues that mounting copyright litigation and legal uncertainty around AI training data could significantly constrain the growth of the generative AI industry.

ip_further_links.title: The User Has Changed. Has Scholarly Publishing?
ip_further_links.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen examines how the rise of AI-driven research tools is transforming user behaviour and asks whether academic publishers are adapting their models fast enough to keep pace.

ip_further_links.title: How Italy's SIAE Is Shaping the Future of Copyright Protection Amid AI
ip_further_links.summary: Italy's collective rights management society SIAE is positioning itself as a key actor in developing copyright frameworks to protect creators from AI-related infringement.

ip_further_links.title: Indonesia Weighs AI Royalty Agency to Protect Creators' Rights
ip_further_links.summary: Indonesia is considering establishing a dedicated AI royalty agency as part of efforts to modernise its intellectual property framework and ensure creators are compensated when their work is used in AI training.
